title: BenevolentAI knowledge graph proposed baricitinib for COVID-19; randomized trials and regulators confirmed benefit
summary: Researchers used the Benevolent Platform to identify baricitinib as a possible treatment before it was tested in clinical trials.
account: On 4 February 2020 BenevolentAI staff published a Lancet correspondence. It reported that the company's machine-learning-built knowledge graph identified baricitinib, a rheumatoid-arthritis JAK inhibitor, as a candidate against 2019-nCoV because it binds AAK1. AAK1 is a regulator of viral endocytosis. Randomized trials tested it. ACTT-2 (1,033 patients, enrolled 8 May to 1 July 2020) reported median recovery of 7 days versus 8 (rate ratio 1.16, 95% CI 1.01–1.32). On high-flow oxygen or non-invasive ventilation, 10 versus 18 days. COV-BARRIER (1,525 patients) missed its primary endpoint of disease progression (27.8% versus 30.5%, odds ratio 0.85, p=0.18). Its 28-day all-cause mortality, a secondary endpoint, was 8% versus 13% (hazard ratio 0.57, nominal p=0.0018). Because the primary endpoint failed, the prespecified procedure did not establish statistical significance for the secondary endpoints after adjustment for multiple testing. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized it with remdesivir on 19 November 2020. WHO strongly recommended it on 14 January 2022. BenevolentAI identifies the discovery system as the Benevolent Platform in its 2022 results, published on 16 March 2023, and dates the baricitinib identification to January 2020.
purpose: Drug repurposing: mine a machine-learning-built biomedical knowledge graph for approved drugs that might block a new coronavirus.
system: Benevolent Platform, using its machine-learning-built knowledge graph and AAK1 inhibitor screening
deployer: ACTT-2 Study Group (NIAID); COV-BARRIER investigators (Eli Lilly)
segment: Hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring supplemental oxygen or ventilatory support
taxonomy_note: The AI's part was candidate identification; the realized good is faster recovery and lower mortality in trials.

ratings.reason: COV-BARRIER reported 28-day all-cause mortality of 8% (62 patients) on baricitinib versus 13% (100 patients) on placebo, hazard ratio 0.57. The randomized comparison supports a life-preserving treatment benefit.
ACTT-2 showed median recovery falling from 8 to 7 days overall and from 18 to 10 days on high-flow oxygen or non-invasive ventilation. That materially eased hospital burden.
WHO strongly recommended baricitinib for severe or critical COVID-19 on 14 January 2022. That made the AI-proposed drug part of standard pandemic care at population scale.

ai_role.statement: The AI's role was hypothesis generation only: BenevolentAI's knowledge graph ranked baricitinib among six high-affinity AAK1-binding approved drugs and the authors published the prediction. It did not design, run or analyze the trials. ACTT-2 was led by NIAID, with input from the drug suppliers. COV-BARRIER was designed with Eli Lilly, which also analyzed the data. These trials tested the drug, not the additional benefit of using AI to identify it. FDA and WHO subsequently assessed the clinical evidence.

versions_and_access.finding: June 18, 2020 correction restores two omitted BenevolentAI authors.
September 8, 2021 correction changes the baricitinib number at risk on day 14 in Figure 2A to 684.

versions_and_access.supplements: Original and final protocols, analysis plans, supplementary methods/results, and Figure S2 were inspected. Patient-level trial data were not reanalyzed.

versions_and_access.status: Full original text, Figure 3 and its description, and methods inspected through Europe PMC XML. Supplementary Table S1 remained inaccessible.

limitations: No trial randomized the discovery process to AI versus no AI. The full proprietary graph and ranking run are unavailable.
COV-BARRIER was sponsor-designed and sponsor-analyzed. Its mortality inference is nominal under the prespecified testing hierarchy.
The cited recommendation establishes guidance, not measured worldwide adoption or a count of lives saved.

The original Sorrell et al. article was read. Its linked supplementary Table S1 was identified, but the download returned 403 or a verification page and the supplementary archive timed out; no unavailable table contents were inferred.

fields.summary: Researchers used the Benevolent Platform to identify baricitinib as a possible treatment before it was tested in clinical trials.
fields.account: On 4 February 2020 BenevolentAI staff published a Lancet correspondence. It reported that the company's machine-learning-built knowledge graph identified baricitinib, a rheumatoid-arthritis JAK inhibitor, as a candidate against 2019-nCoV because it binds AAK1. AAK1 is a regulator of viral endocytosis. Randomized trials tested it. ACTT-2 (1,033 patients, enrolled 8 May to 1 July 2020) reported median recovery of 7 days versus 8 (rate ratio 1.16, 95% CI 1.01–1.32). On high-flow oxygen or non-invasive ventilation, 10 versus 18 days. COV-BARRIER (1,525 patients) missed its primary endpoint of disease progression (27.8% versus 30.5%, odds ratio 0.85, p=0.18). Its 28-day all-cause mortality, a secondary endpoint, was 8% versus 13% (hazard ratio 0.57, nominal p=0.0018). Because the primary endpoint failed, the prespecified procedure did not establish statistical significance for the secondary endpoints after adjustment for multiple testing. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized it with remdesivir on 19 November 2020. WHO strongly recommended it on 14 January 2022. BenevolentAI identifies the discovery system as the Benevolent Platform in its 2022 results, published on 16 March 2023, and dates the baricitinib identification to January 2020.
